subject: MSA & Order Form redlines — IP ownership / training carveouts
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Jane Park <jane.park@curelylabs.com>, Procurement <procurement@curelylabs.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-01T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: MSA & Order Form redlines — IP ownership / training carveouts

Hi Jane / Curely procurement team,

Thanks for the productive call this morning. Attached is a redlined MSA and an updated order form (high level) that reflect the items we discussed: a) ownership of customer outputs, b) narrow training opt-out / feedback license, and c) telemetry/evidence requests for productization.

High-level asks from Curely I noted:
- You want assignment of output IP for the specific product integration (proposed by your side).
- Tight limits on Redwood using any customer data or outputs to train models commercially.
- A mechanism for evidentiary telemetry if Curely later requests handoff/evidence for IP claims.

Where we stand (Redwood view):
- We typically license outputs to customers under a broad, perpetual, nonexclusive license but do not assign model IP. We are open to a limited assignment for specific deliverables if narrowly scoped and subject to audit/evidence gating.
- Training: we can exclude identifiable customer data from aggregate training when requested (opt-out), and propose a mutually agreed Exhibit that lists scope and timing.
- Feedback license: we need a limited, irrevocable feedback license so we can improve the runtime and safety; propose language that restricts commercial use of customer prompts/outputs for model training unless customer explicitly opts in.

Next steps I propose:
1) Laura (cc'ed) to propose compromise redline language for the MSA that preserves our runtime/ops needs while addressing Curely's productization concerns.
2) If Curely can confirm the set of deliverables they expect assigned (if any), we can scope an Exhibit and timeline.
3) Agree on procurement signoff date — Curely suggested end of next week on the call; please confirm.

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_redline.docx | OrderForm_Draft.pdf (attached as stubs below)

Thanks,

Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Jane Park <jane.park@curelylabs.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@curelylabs.com>
Date: 2025-08-01T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form redlines — IP ownership / training carveouts

Hi Stephanie,

Appreciate the summary and the draft redline. We've reviewed internally and a few clarifying points before Laura submits formal language:

1) On assignment vs. license: Curely's product roadmap assumes ownership for the generated outputs that are directly produced and consumed by our product (e.g., responses shipped to our end users). We understand your licensing stance; can you confirm whether Redwood would consider a time-limited assignment for a defined set of deliverables (we proposed Exhibit A on the call) in exchange for a higher commitment level on reserved capacity?

2) Training: our concern is downstream model commercialization. We need strong contractual assurance that Redwood will not use Curely data (prompts, outputs, private docs) to train models used by other customers. An opt-out that is acknowledged but with broad escape clauses is insufficient. We would accept a specific carveout with narrow exceptions (security patches, safety fixes) and clear notice requirements.

3) Feedback license: Curely can grant a very limited telemetry/bugfix license, but not a general "improvements" license. Any telemetry used should be de-identified and only for operational improvements to the Redwood service.

I've attached our redline for reference (highlights on sections 7, 12, and Exhibit A). Please review and let us know if Laura's counterproposal will address these three points. We are aiming to finalize contract terms by 2025-08-08 to meet our launch timing.

Best,

Jane Park
Senior Counsel, Curely Labs
[Attachment: Novum_redline_MSA.docx (docx)]

Date: 2025-08-02T09:48:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Re: MSA & Order Form redlines — IP ownership / training carveouts

Laura / Legal team,

Forwarding Curely's redline and the ask list. Their three main non-negotiables are assignment for certain deliverables, a strong training exclusion, and a very limited telemetry/feedback license.

Ben — appreciate if you can quantify what Curely's ask for reserved capacity (they mentioned higher commitment) would translate to in ARR / GPU-days so we can show tradeoffs.

Suggested legal approach:
- Offer a narrow assignment for "Productized Deliverables" defined in Exhibit A (customer provides single list, time-limited to 24 months, subject to fees and evidence audit).
- Training: accept explicit opt-out for production data; add a carveout for safety/security fixes with strict minimization and notice.
- Feedback license: convert to a limited operational license that permits de-identified telemetry and bugfixes only; prohibit use for model training without explicit opt-in.

Please draft proposed MSA snippets and an Exhibit A template. Curely expects signoff by 2025-08-08; they flagged launch dependencies.

Thanks,

Stephanie

Hi Jane, Stephanie,

Thanks — attached is a proposed counter (text excerpt + attachments) that tries to balance Curely's productization concerns with Redwood's need to operate and improve the service.

Key proposed language (excerpt):
"Productized Deliverables" means discrete outputs produced solely for Customer in connection with Services and identified in Exhibit A. For such Productized Deliverables, Redwood hereby grants and assigns to Customer a worldwide, perpetual, royalty-free right in the deliverable materials as delivered. Assignment shall be limited to the deliverable materials and shall not include underlying model weights, training data, or Redwood's pre-existing materials.

Training / Use of Customer Data: Redwood shall not use Customer Content or outputs identified in Exhibit A to further train any foundation model for commercial use for other customers. Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for operational improvements and safety fixes; any use beyond that requires Customer's explicit written opt-in.

Feedback/Telemetry License: Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive license to use de-identified telemetry and feedback solely for debugging, performance monitoring, and safety fixes. Such license does not permit model training unless Customer opts in via Exhibit A.

Attachments included: redwood_counter_MSALanguage.txt (contains full snippet for Sections 7 & 12), OrderForm_ExhibitA_changes.pdf (template for listing Productized Deliverables), and a sample evidence checklist for telemetry requests.

Next steps:
- Jane / Curely: please review the attached counter and confirm whether Exhibit A template and the 24-month assignment window are acceptable. We can then prepare a short side letter describing reserved capacity / pricing tradeoffs.
- Ben / Sales ops to provide committed capacity numbers and pricing by EOD 2025-08-04 so Curely can weigh the exchange.

If agreeable, I'll prepare a clean MSA with tracked changes for final review.

Regards,

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
